newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore gas oil trades close to five-year high.
newsitem.headline: Singapore gas oil trades close to five-year high.

text.p: Singapore oil gas oil prices firmed on Thursday to trade near its previous five-year high on renewed demand for prompt cargoes and a stronger crude and product market in London, traders said.

A 150,000-barrel cargo loading in late November traded between a European major and a Singapore trader at $30.50 a barrel, five cents off its previous five-year high in mid October. An early December cargo was bid at $30.35 a barrel against an offer at $30.55.
November gas oil swaps traded at $30.35, up sharply from Wednesday's $29.70/$29.80.
Traders said firmer Singapore gas oil prices also opened the arbitrage for one Northwest European and two Mediterranean cargoes to be fixed for delivery to India in December.

Jet fuel came under selling pressure following the purchase of two jet fuel December cargoes by Taiwan at relatively low prices and increased supplies, traders said. Taiwan bought two 32,000-tonne cargoes at $241-$242 a tonne c+f, about $3 below market expectations, they said.
A 120,000-barrel December 2-6 cargo traded at $30.20 a barrel fob Singapore while a 100,000-barrel lot traded at $30.15 for early Decemner lifting fob.
Jet fuel prices were also hit by arbitrage cargoes from the U.S. West Coast and Venezuela to cover Japanese winter demand despite high stocks in Guam and China, traders said.

Gasoline edged up with crude. An offer for 50,000 barrels of 95-octane unleaded was seen at $24.90 a barrel fob Singapore for December 3-5. Low 92-octane, said to be in greater surplus than the higher grades, was steady and traded at $24.00.
Naphtha was unchanged in quiet trade at $22.20/22.55.
Fuel oil firmed on continued buying from a Singapore trader, for a 20,000-tonne cargo at $119.00 a tonne. Chinese demand emerged for December arrival.
